newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Aide defends Argentina's Fernandez from Cavallo.
newsitem.headline: Aide defends Argentina's Fernandez from Cavallo.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez's cabinet chief defended his boss Wednesday against criticisms of "weakness" and worse by his predecessor, Domingo Cavallo.

Cavallo, sacked in July, has called his successor "either dishonest or incapable" for appearing to endorse a businessman Cavallo accuses of graft. Cavallo withdrew this in a meeting with business leaders Tuesday, but said instead Fernandez "is weak and weakness shows itself in higher public spending..."
Fernandez's Cabinet Chief Carlos Rodriguez told reporters not to confuse his boss's low-profile style with weakness or Cavallo's confrontational style with decisiveness.

"Roque Fernandez has a different style to Cavallo. But don't confuse Cavallo's frontal shock tactics with powers of decision," said Rodriguez, underlining former Central Bank chief Fernandez's "consensual, reasoning, analytical" style.

Rodriguez challenged Cavallo's allegation that Fernandez was letting public spending slip and questioned Cavallo's own record on fiscal discipline -- pointing out that though he presented a tight budget last year, he did not keep to it.

"You can be as tough as you like and get your budget passed, but then you cannot execute the budget, like last year," said the official. "There is tough and there is tough, but the proof of the pudding is in the eating."
Rodriguez warned Cavallo that his criticisms of Fernandez were "making noise" that could drive up Argentina's country risk, and advised him as an economist to stick to economics.
"Cavallo is strong on political criticism, but now as a private citizen he should make economic criticisms."
